orphans: the document record itself (notice, specification, evaluation report, award decision, amendments) — every column holds claims derived from documents, none holds the documents
the chronology — event sequence is the evidence in a procurement story; no column and no field holds order, and mechanisms[].chain is causal by design
the governing rule and its citation — the standard the conduct is measured against, distinct from politics-as-event
right of reply — responses obtained and responses refused
column_utilisation.note: Contradicts the orchestrator's column-collapse hypothesis. All seven hold, three (the-number, macro, politics) only after re-labelling column content, which is `content` by the rubric's own definition and is reported as such rather than inflated.

Two line items get WORSE: scoping absences by hand (no field) and the legal register pass (a conclusions section the machinery cannot police must be read line by line). Confidence low per accepted-gaps.md `scope-note`: no runner exists, so this measures the methodic as written.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only — no real case named)
findings.title: An established absence cannot be recorded as one — facts[] has no polarity, and neither unknowns[] nor research_gaps[] is its home
findings.expected: A record that should exist, which the run established does not, is affirmative evidence and must be recordable as such — marked as an absence, with an evidence label that says a negative result was established rather than a positive one observed.
findings.got: unknowns[] is defined by its restrictive `impact` — 'it tells the script what it may not say' (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:77) and Rule 5 at :98-99 — so filing an absence there inverts its polarity from licence to muzzle. research_gaps[] is 'what the run did NOT do' (:88-89, RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:110-113) — a confession of effort, so filing an absence there converts the finding into the reporter's own failure and hands the subject their defence. facts[] (:42) accepts the claim string and loses polarity entirely: an absence renders identically to a positive fact at every downstream step, including CARD_DIMENSION (dimensions.ts:50-60) and the beat chain. Neither evidence vocabulary in the repo (confidence high|medium|low at :46; MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED/EXTERNAL at DIRECTOR-DIMENSION.md:9-10) has a rung for a negative result.
findings.refuter_pass: Tried all four. (a) Is this the topic being hard? No — an established absence is evidence in any domain with an official record, and RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:48 already names 'the absent thing' as a tension shape, so the methodic knows absences exist and only supports them at tension level. (b) Would a competent execution produce this anyway? A competent researcher writes the absence into facts[] as a string — which is the smuggling route, not a repair; the loss is structural, not performance-dependent. (c) Present somewhere unread? Searched the whole methodic for absence/missing/negative — RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:48 and ENGINES.md:46 are the only hits and neither is a field. (d) lens or content? content — the reference run's own f-sbr-unbuilt is an absence, so the incumbent market topic needs this too; it merely got the easy case where a party admitted it.
findings.l2_priority: Attempt to write an established absence into a real notebook and observe which field it lands in and how the rendered script narrates it. Specifically: does the script assert the absence as a finding, or hedge it?

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only)
findings.title: No field for the scope of a negative search — an absence claim is unfalsifiable without the universe that was searched
findings.expected: An absence claim carries the boundary of the search that established it: which register, which period, which names, which request reference, what the response was. Scope is what makes a negative checkable, and a checkable negative is the difference between reporting and insinuation.
findings.got: facts[] is {id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?} (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:42), and Rule 2 at :94 demands 'every fact dated and sourced. No exceptions.' Where an authority answers 'no such document is held', the response is a source and the rule is satisfiable. Where the absence is established by exhaustive search of a public register, or by silence, there is no source and the rule cannot be met honestly — so the scope goes in the free-text `note` or nowhere. confidence (:46) also collapses two separable propositions: confidence that the record is missing, and confidence that it should have existed. The second is the contested one and is argued from the governing rule, for which there is also no field (see pc-06).
findings.refuter_pass: Distinct from pc-01 and deliberately not merged: pc-01 asks for a polarity marker, this asks for a provenance sub-shape, and they force different edits — a fix for one does not fix the other. Refuted the 'note? field covers it' objection: an unstructured note is not consumed by any composition step, which by the schema's own principle (:8-9) means it does not belong as the carrier of a load-bearing constraint.
findings.l2_priority: Where does the scope of a negative search actually end up in a produced notebook, and does the script inherit it or drop it?

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only)
findings.title: The leap ladder measures distance from evidence, not distance from an accusation — and no Conclusion field names who the claim is about
findings.expected: A synthesis layer that can produce claims about identifiable living people should be able to record that it has done so, so any policy — a naming rule, an escalation, a UI marker, a future validator — has something to fire on. Legal jeopardy should be an axis, not an accident of inferential distance.
findings.got: Leap is `near | moderate | far | unhinged` (conclusions.ts:26) and LEAP_NOTE (:28-34) defines every tier purely as distance from the evidence. Those axes are orthogonal: 'the award did not comply with the applicable procurement rule' is a NEAR leap — barely a restatement of the cards — and is simultaneously a legal conclusion reserved to a body empowered to make it. The ladder therefore scores the most dangerous claim in this domain at the tier with the least scrutiny, and illegality is not tiered at all because it is not a motive claim and so never reaches `unhinged`. Underneath: interface Conclusion (:36-60) carries id, claim, reasoning, leap, restsOn, precedent, falsifiableBy, useFor, hottest — restsOn names cards, useFor names placement, and NOTHING names a subject. Defamation exposure is a function of who a claim is about; the data model cannot represent that axis.
findings.refuter_pass: The strongest refutation available is that three real safeguards already exist and I credit all three: opt-in asymmetry (:14-16), the mandatory falsifier (:17-19, :49-50), and the higher bar plus UI marking on `hottest` (:55-58). They survive the challenge — they are aimed at whether a claim is TRUE. The finding is narrower and survives them: they are calibrated for truth-status, exposure is a function of subject identifiability, and no field records identifiability. Also checked against accepted-gaps.md `by-design` ('conclusions have no sources') — this is not that complaint and is not suppressed by it. lens vs content: content, and emphatically — a `subjects[]` field on a shared interface serves the financial-fraud, security-breach, sanctions and electoral seats identically, and a fraud-only lens would leave the other nineteen shipping motive claims about named people with no handle on it.
findings.l2_priority: Produce a conclusion about a named living person and have the exposure review state what a lawyer would strike. Then check whether anything in the notebook or UI could have flagged it in advance.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only)
findings.title: The top leap tier is DEFINED as a motive claim and framed as a reward, and the falsifier tests the checkable half of a sentence whose dangerous half is uncheckable by construction
findings.expected: A tier that permits imputing motive to identifiable people should read as a hazard with conditions, not as an incentive. Its falsifier should reach the imputation, or the design should state plainly that it cannot and gate the tier on subject identifiability instead.
findings.got: LEAP_NOTE.unhinged (conclusions.ts:32-33): 'The hottest take. A claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is — nobody can source what someone intended. Entertaining, defensible as speculation, indefensible as fact.' The tier is not permissive of motive claims, it is defined as one, and the framing ('hottest', 'entertaining') is an incentive gradient pointing at the exact cliff a fraud-beat exposure bar forbids. It ships: c-reserve-was-the-product (:163-179) imputes motive to an identifiable administration and identifiable donors. Its falsifier (:175-176), 'a funded, audited reserve with a published coin count', is genuinely checkable and IS a document — so the falsifier rule is doing real work — but it refutes the observable shell (nothing was built), not the imputation (it was never meant to be built). The file concedes the imputation is unsourceable at :33 and permits it at :32 in the same breath.
findings.refuter_pass: Kept separate from pc-03 because the edits differ: pc-03 adds a field, this rewrites a tier definition and its incentive framing. Refuted 'the falsifier requirement already constrains it adequately' — the orchestrator's third lead — only partially, and I am contradicting the lead in BOTH directions: the falsifier is not a fig leaf here (it is checkable, and documentary in the worked case), but adequacy fails because a motive falsifier can only ever test the observable proxy. Marked present-broken rather than confirmed-absent: the safeguard exists and does not reach.
findings.l2_priority: Does an `unhinged` conclusion get generated unprompted on a topic with named living subjects, and does the framing of the tier make it more likely?

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only)
findings.title: Right of reply is nowhere in the methodic, and no fact can be marked must-carry
findings.expected: Any run producing claims about an identifiable person or organisation should be instructed to seek their response, and their silence should be recordable as a dated, sourced fact that cannot be silently descoped.
findings.got: 'right of reply', 'for comment', 'declined to comment', 'allege', 'defam', 'libel' return no relevant hit anywhere in RESEARCH-PROMPT.md, NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md, ENGINES.md, CRAFT-BASELINE.md or conclusions.ts. Nine prompt phases (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:20-113) and a ten-item quality bar (:119-130) never mention approaching a subject, so a notebook can pass every stated check and never have contacted the person it is about. Recording a refusal is possible only by smuggling it into facts[] with source='own correspondence' — workable, unmarked, and voluntary. counter_positions_to_state_fairly[] (:74) is the intuitive home and is wrong: a position a named official declined to state is the absence of a position, not one. And because facts are in scope until cut by design (conclusions.ts:14-16) with no must-carry flag, the one line that makes the piece defensible is as descopable as any other card. The nearest thing in the whole library to a conflict declaration is ENGINES.md:129, 'it must disclose the author's exposure', confined to Engine E.
findings.refuter_pass: (a) Topic being hard? No — every seat whose topic names a company or a person needs this, which is most of the cast. (b) Competent execution? A competent journalist does it from habit; the methodic neither prompts it nor protects it, and habit is not a mechanism. (c) Present but missed? Grepped the full methodic; confirmed-absent. (d) The must-carry half genuinely challenges a philosophy commitment ('opt-in asymmetry', 'the wound graph'), so I state it as narrowly as it deserves: not that facts should stop being descopable, but that ONE flag should exist saying a cut has consequences outside the argument.
findings.l2_priority: Run the exposure review on a produced notebook and check whether a right-of-reply line exists at all without being asked for.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only)
findings.title: No register separation between a descriptive irregularity and a normative or adjudicative claim — and `tension` actively invites the collapse
findings.expected: The notebook should distinguish 'the specification named a proprietary product' (descriptive) from 'the specification breached the neutrality rule' (normative) from 'the award was unlawful' (adjudicative), and should pin any normative claim to the cited rule it is measured against.
findings.got: The schema sees one string called `claim` (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:42) and no field records the register or the governing standard. `tension` is {expectation, reality, why_it_is_a_tension} (:33-34); for a procurement topic the most natural and most persuasive filling of `expectation` is what the RULES REQUIRE, which produces a well-formed tension that is one adjective from an allegation, and RESEARCH-PROMPT.md Phase 2 (:37-52) gives no register guidance — all five tension shapes at :42-49 are descriptive by construction. The register shift then happens invisibly in free-text `note`, exactly as modelled by the reference run's f-sbr-unbuilt ('The flagship policy win is, in practice, unimplemented. Strong irony beat.'), where a descriptive fact acquires its rhetorical framing in an unreviewable field the script inherits. Related: no column and no field carries the governing rule and its citation (orphan O3), so a claim about non-compliance cannot name what it is non-compliant with.
findings.refuter_pass: Absorbed a weaker finding I dropped here: that mechanisms[].chain cannot hold a timeline. That was refuted as by-design — RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:65-67 deliberately excludes sequences and CRAFT-BASELINE.md:13-32 is the repo's central law — and survives only as column orphan O2, noted because the pressure to convert a chronology into a mechanism IS a register-escalation pressure specific to this domain. The finding as scored stands on the missing register field, not on the timeline complaint.
findings.l2_priority: Read the produced script and mark every sentence as descriptive / normative / adjudicative. Count how many normative claims arrived without a cited standard.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only)
findings.title: Engine selection has no exposure axis — engine_fit is material fit only, and the engine most hazardous to a named subject carries no warning
findings.expected: An engine catalogue used on topics involving named people should record, per engine, what its structure costs when the subject can sue — not only whether the material fits it.
findings.got: engine_fit[] is {engine, fit, why, recommended?}, 'assessed from the MATERIAL, not from taste' (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:80-82). Material fit is the only axis, so nothing can record 'this engine fits and must not be used on this subject'. Concretely: Engine G · Paradox Teaser (ENGINES.md:144-156) is 'flat contradiction, repeated → the reveal → the absurd detail' — applied to a named official that is insinuation with a runtime, producing the imputation in the viewer while leaving nothing on the page to defend, and it carries no warning. Engine D terminates in a verdict about named conduct (:70); its D-honest tells (:81-96) are a genuine asset but they police the fairness of the WEIGHING, never the REGISTER of the verdict. The catalogue proves it can do this: the note at :103-112 distinguishes persuasion techniques from explanation techniques at length — for Engine D alone.
findings.refuter_pass: Explicitly content and not lens: ENGINES.md:11-12 states the catalogue is 'open, not settled', so adding an axis and adding entries is the mechanism working as designed. Refuted the stronger version of my own complaint — that Engine D is unsafe for this domain — since the D-honest tells are a real safety asset and D remains structurally the cleanest fit for the material; the gap is the register of its verdict, not the engine.
findings.l2_priority: Render the notebook through D and through A and compare which produces more sentences the exposure review strikes.

findings.title: No engine's payoff is an unresolved question placed on the record
findings.expected: An engine for the form 'here is what the documents show, here is what has been explained, here is what has not' — where the honest ending is that the question is now public and unanswered.
findings.got: All seven engines resolve: A, C and F end in a reframe, D in a verdict, B in a payoff, E in guidance, G in a tease. The catalogue's fallback (ENGINES.md:171) is 'none of these → not a video yet — it is a topic; go find the tension', which mis-diagnoses a piece whose tension is real and whose resolution is legally unavailable. Partial mitigation, and the reason this scores minor rather than major: Engine B · Effort/Payoff Gap (:44-54) is a genuinely good fit — the labour of the request process against a redacted page — and its beat 'notice what's missing' (:46) is the only phrase in the entire methodic that treats an absence as a beat. Nothing in the methodic would surface B for this material, because engine_fit assesses subject fit and B reads as a comedy engine.
findings.refuter_pass: Downgraded from major to minor and from confirmed to uncertain on the refuter pass: I found a working engine (B) for my own material while writing the objection, which substantially weakens 'no engine renders this'. Left open because the discovery was accidental and nothing in the methodic points at it — which may itself be a discoverability finding against `knowledge` rather than a taxonomy gap. L2 should decide.
findings.l2_priority: Render through B and judge whether an unresolved ending survives as a payoff or reads as a failure.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only)
findings.title: confidence collapses authenticity, provenance and interest — a primary document from the party under scrutiny rates `high`
findings.expected: A source that is primary AND self-serving should be representable as both. Authenticity and reliability are different questions.
findings.got: facts[].confidence is high|medium|low (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:46) with one named demotion rule: 'Vendor research is `low` by default'. An authority's own response about its own conduct is a primary document of unimpeachable authenticity and the account of an interested party — under one enum it rates `high`, correctly as to the first and dangerously as to the second, and the vendor rule does not generalise to a public body. This domain's evidence floor is otherwise HIGH — tender notices and registry filings are primary where the reference run's own research_gaps concedes 'every figure remains aggregator-sourced' — so this is a precision gap, not a demotion gap.
findings.refuter_pass: This is the finding that CONTRADICTS the orchestrator's evidence-ladder lead for my domain, and I record it that way deliberately: my best material is primary and the methodic does not demote it. Also corrects the lead's scope — the MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder (DIRECTOR-DIMENSION.md:9-10) labels the LIBRARY's own methodological claims, inside a document whose header states 'Nothing here is implemented' (:3); it is never applied to notebook facts, so it cannot demote a domain's material.
findings.l2_priority: Confirm what confidence a real FOI response receives, and whether the script treats it as neutral testimony.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: A public procurement award whose documents, timeline and winner's history sit oddly together (shape only)
findings.title: No instruction to establish a base rate — for any 'is this unusual?' topic the base rate IS the counter-case's evidence
findings.expected: Where the counter-case is 'nothing unusual is happening', Phase 1 should ask for the population this instance belongs to: how often this pattern occurs ordinarily, in comparable cases.
findings.got: The counter-case row is mandatory and well specified (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:32-35), reinforced by dimensions.ts:36-37 marking the empty column 'DANGEROUS', by the mandatory steel_man (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:61-65), and by D-honest tell 1 (ENGINES.md:87-90) requiring the premise itself in the candidate set. The reference run executes it honestly. But the string 'base rate' appears NOWHERE in the methodic, steel_man.evidence[] points at fact ids (:62), and the reference run populates it entirely from facts internal to the case. Nothing tells a researcher the counter-case may need evidence the case does not contain. For this topic the ordinary-explanation reading — the authority has no procurement specialist, the deadline was set by a funding window, the supplier market is genuinely thin — is only weighable against comparison numbers from outside the award.
findings.refuter_pass: Contradicts the orchestrator's fourth lead: the counter-case requirement is NOT unsatisfiable for this topic — it is the best-served criterion in the whole pass and is scored as a pass. Downgraded to minor accordingly, and marked present-but-missed rather than confirmed-absent, because Phase 1's macro row could hold base rates under a re-label and a competent researcher might get there unaided. Recorded as one row of the domain table, which is precisely the `content` fix the rubric describes.
findings.l2_priority: Did the run seek any comparison population for the counter-case, or only case-internal evidence?
